audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read Skill on all seven rows while the content layer and the packet both read Aurora everywhere except level 6. Two answers to the same question on one page. enemyWin also claimed Annie is 'out-ranging your plan'.
audit.why: Annie's longest spell is Disintegrate at 625; Incinerate is 600 and Tibbers casts at 600. Aurora's Q is 900 and her E is 825. The range advantage is Aurora's by a wide margin, which is exactly why the lane is hers outside the level 6 window.
audit.corrected: Aurora at 1, 2, 3, 4-5 (4/10), Annie at 6 (6/10), Aurora at first item and two items (5/10) — the full layer's sides, ratings and whys moved onto the content and packet chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was right in direction but carried no numbers, and the late spike was argued from 'Between Worlds gives you a clean way to dodge her Tibbers/stun engage' — Aurora's R has no dodge, no phase and no untargetability.
audit.why: Tibbers is 130s at rank 1 falling to 100s at rank 3 and casts at 600 range; Annie has no dash at all. Late, the spike is that she has to walk into a fight Aurora can slow the ground of.
audit.corrected: 6 tips to Annie on a stocked stun into a 600-range Tibbers. Late tips back because a 100s ult on an immobile champion has to be walked into range.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit R cooldown and range, ownerKit R text)

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly described Pyromania as needing 'four spell hits' or a 'four-hit stun combo'. Riot's text says after casting 4 SPELLS her next offensive spell stuns — the casts do not have to hit you, and they can be spent on the wave. It also never mentioned that Annie begins the game and respawns with Pyromania already available, nor that Molten Shield damages enemies who strike her with attacks or spells.
audit.why: A player who thinks he can deny the stun by dodging will walk into it while she stacks on minions, and a player who bursts into a fresh Molten Shield pays for the shield twice.
audit.corrected: Four of her own casts stock the stun; the glow under her feet is the tell. She has it available at level 1 and after every respawn. Force Molten Shield (10s) out with a Q before you commit the pattern.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit P/E text and cooldowns)

notes:
Level chart: the full layer read Skill on all seven rows while content and packet.levelChart agreed with each other on Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Annie/Aurora/Aurora. Two agreeing sources against one flat template, so I moved the full layer onto them — side, rating and why together per row. The content win[] rows were already correct and untouched.

The biggest factual correction here is not the chart: the page described Pyromania as a 'four-hit stun combo' in three places. Riot's text is four CASTS, which she can spend on minions, so nothing the Aurora player does with mobility denies the stun. The tell is the glow, and the page did have that phrase in one field — it just contradicted itself elsewhere.

Unverified and left alone: whether Tibbers persists to keep attacking after Annie dies, and whether his aura damage is what actually threatens Aurora post-hop. Riot's text says only that Tibbers can attack and burns enemies near him; the kit file has nothing on his duration or his behaviour on her death, so I wrote nothing about it.

No pronoun risk missed as far as I can tell: every remaining he/his in the untouched fields belongs to report[7], report[10] and report[12], which contain none.
